findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod SafeParseReturnType (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token. The old code `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the token itself. This result is now written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the DB holds `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. On the next instantiation, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` throws. Every Google Calendar credential breaks after its first refresh, in both normal and sync mode. Use `key.data` (or `.parse`).

findings.title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response, which callers expecting SDK/axios shapes cannot use
findings.body:
In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response`. In normal mode it returns whatever the provider-specific function returns, and several callers depend on that shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws.
- HubSpot treats the result as a `TokenResponseIF`. It computes `expiryDate` from `undefined * 1000` (NaN) and persists the Response object as the credential key.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape) and throw a TypeError.
- Lark goes through `handleLarkError`, which expects `{code:0,data:{...}}`.
- Webex validates with a strict schema that requires `scope`, `refresh_token_expires_in`, etc.

None of these work with the documented sync response ("only the access token and expiry date"). Credential sync is effectively broken for most of the apps this PR wires up.

findings.title: Computed schema keys evaluate to "[object Object]", so expiry fields are stripped in sync mode
findings.body:
`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". The second overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, so `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and every other field from the sync endpoint is dropped.

Consequences in sync mode:
- Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined*1000)` = NaN. The stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema` on next use.
- Office365 never updates expiry, so it refreshes on every call.
- Salesforce loses `instance_url`.

Use `.passthrough()`, or an explicit schema with the expected expiry field.

findings.title: Placeholder "refresh_token" string overwrites real stored refresh tokens
findings.body:
When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 then does `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and persists the result, replacing the user's real refresh token with the string "refresh_token". This happens whenever Microsoft omits a refresh token (the schema marks it optional) and always in sync mode.

Zoom in sync mode likewise sets `key.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Before this change, a missing refresh token left the existing one intact. Now the credential becomes unrefreshable once the sync endpoint is turned off. Don't inject a fake value; let callers keep the existing refresh token.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file imports nothing from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a type error at build time and a ReferenceError at runtime. `getClient` therefore always rejects, which breaks every Salesforce operation (create, update, delete event and contact search).

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation but builds the connection with the stale token
findings.body:
`getClient` now requests a new access token from login.salesforce.com every time the service is constructed, with no expiry check. That costs an extra network round trip and adds rate-limit pressure on every booking.

The freshly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is saved to the DB, but `jsforce.Connection` is still built from `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` (the old values). The refresh therefore has no effect on the current request.

This path also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it never uses the sync endpoint. Yet `parseRefreshTokenResponse` applies the minimal schema in sync mode, which drops `instance_url` from the persisted key.

findings.title: Success check relies on `statusText === "OK"` instead of `response.ok`
findings.body: HTTP/2 and some proxies return an empty or different reason phrase. A successful 200 response can then be treated as an error, and the HttpError message is empty. Use `response.ok` or check the status code.

findings.title: Credential ID is passed as the user ID to the credential sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key where the other callers pass `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credentialId>`, so it returns tokens for whichever user happens to have that ID. Those tokens are then written into this credential, giving the wrong Cal.com user access to another user's Zoho Bigin account. `credential.userId` needs to be threaded into `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: Wrong app slug "zoomvideo" sent to the sync endpoint
findings.body: The Zoom app slug, used as `appId` when the credential is created, is "zoom"; "zoomvideo" is only the directory name. The self-hosted sync endpoint receives `appSlug=zoomvideo`, which won't match the slug used everywhere else, including the inbound webhook that looks apps up by slug. Token refresh for Zoom fails in sync mode.

findings.title: `appStoreMetadata` is indexed by slug, but its keys are directory names
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365video`). The handler indexes it with `app.slug` (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `zoom`, `msteams`). For every app whose slug differs from its dirName, the lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found". Most of the apps this feature targets therefore can't be synced. Select `dirName` from the `App` row and index by that.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
findings.body: The shared secret that authorizes writing arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user is compared with plain string inequality, which leaks timing information. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Also reject requests where the header is missing or is an array.

findings.title: Invalid body or undecryptable keys cause unhandled 500s; no method check
findings.body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or key. Neither is caught, so the caller gets a generic 500 instead of a 400. The handler also accepts any HTTP method, not just POST. Use `safeParse`, wrap decryption in try/catch, and return 400/405 as appropriate.

findings.title: Updating synced keys does not clear the credential's `invalid` flag
findings.body: Credentials get marked `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant` (Google, Zoom, Webex). When the parent platform pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated. The credential stays flagged invalid and is still treated as broken. Set `invalid: false` alongside the new key.

findings.title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
findings.body:
Cal.com POSTs `{calcomUserId, appSlug}` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no secret header and no signature. The endpoint is expected to answer with plaintext access tokens. The self-hosted endpoint has no way to verify the caller is Cal.com, so anyone who can reach it can enumerate user IDs and harvest third-party access tokens.

The inbound direction requires a webhook secret and encrypted payloads, so this is asymmetric. At minimum, send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the configured header.

findings.title: Feature flag constant holds the encryption key itself rather than a boolean
findings.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` evaluates to the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both env vars are set. It is exported from a widely imported constants module. Any place that logs, serializes or returns this "flag" would leak the AES key. Coerce it with `!!(...)`.

findings.title: No tests for the new webhook or the refresh/parse helpers
findings.body: The PR adds an authenticated credential-write webhook and changes token-refresh persistence for about ten integrations, with no unit or integration tests. The description states tests were not added or run. Basic tests would have caught several of the bugs above: the SafeParse wrapper persisted as the Google key, the "[object Object]" schema keys, the missing prisma import, and the slug/dirName mismatch.
